content.todaysFocus: At week 10, Avi brings his hands to his mouth on purpose and inspects them with interest. This week is built for hands-and-mouth sensory play: give him varied surfaces to mouth and narrate what he is feeling.

actionItems.body: Assemble a rotating tray of three safe textured objects today: a silicone teether, a soft fabric book, and a smooth wooden ring. Avoid anything with small loose parts, which remain a choking hazard at this age.
actionItems.sourceLabel: AAP HealthyChildren: baby ages and stages

actionItems.body: Keep cumulative tummy time at 60-plus minutes per day, staggered into four to six short bouts; he should be pushing up on his forearms with his chest off the floor.
actionItems.sourceLabel: AAP: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

actionItems.body: Continue logging feeds and outputs in whatever app you use; you will want a clean record on hand if any fever workup comes up before day 90.

watchFors: [low concern] Profuse drooling and constant hand-sucking. This reflects salivary-gland maturation, not necessarily teething; first teeth typically arrive at 6 to 10 months.

[monitor] Persistent head asymmetry or a favored head-turn to one side (positional plagiocephaly or torticollis). Vary which shoulder you hold him against and raise it at the next visit if it is not resolving.
[call within 24h] Decreased feeding lasting 24 hours or more, or any new color change during feeds.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, an apnea episode, seizure-like activity, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 for blue lips and do not wait!

enrichment.body: Offer the silicone teether, fabric book, and wooden ring one at a time and let him mouth and grip each; varied surfaces build the tactile map his fingers will rely on later.
Let him bring his hands to his mouth and study them during floor time; this self-exploration is the cognitive front edge of the hand-eye coordination that tummy time keeps reinforcing.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

enrichment.body: Narrate each texture as he mouths it (soft, bumpy, smooth, cool); pairing words to sensation feeds the serve-and-return loop linked to stronger later language outcomes.

upcoming: Day 57-72 (post-vaccine window): low-grade fussiness, drowsiness, or mild fever after the 2-month shots should be fully past by now; a new fever is treated as non-vaccine and warrants a same-day call.
Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; start firming up a consistent sleep-wake routine.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).

content.todaysFocus: Sleep is near its most predictable in the 8-to-14-week window, so this is the week to chain a fixed wind-down. A repeatable sequence becomes the cue that tells Avi sleep is next.

actionItems.body: Lock in a fixed three-step wind-down tonight (bath, then one book, then a lights-out song) in the same order every evening; a consistent sequence builds the sleep-onset association that anchors as his pattern stabilizes by 12 to 14 weeks.
actionItems.sourceLabel: AAP HealthyChildren: getting your baby to sleep

actionItems.body: Note last wake time, time he fell asleep, and nap length for the next several days so you can see his emerging wake windows before committing to clock times.
Aim the last nap to end by 16:30 to 17:00 so bedtime can land around 18:30 to 19:30 without overtiredness amplifying night wakings.

watchFors: [low concern] Non-painful spit-up after feeds, decreasing in volume as the upper esophageal sphincter matures.
[monitor] No reliable social smile by now; document it and flag it at the next visit.
[call within 24h] A new persistent crying pattern or a feeding refusal that runs more than 24 hours.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, seizure-like activity, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 for blue lips!

enrichment.body: Chain bath, book, and the lights-out song into one fixed nightly sequence; the predictability itself is what trains sleep onset as his rhythm consolidates by 12 to 14 weeks.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP HealthyChildren: getting your baby to sleep

enrichment.body: Read the same calm wind-down book at the same point each night; the repeated prosody becomes a recognizable signal and seeds early literacy at the same time.
Track last wake, fall-asleep time, and nap length across a few days to surface his natural windows before you try to anchor a loose schedule.

upcoming: Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; the routine you set this week becomes the backbone of it.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).
Around week 14-18: the 4-month sleep regression is on the horizon, after which a sturdy wind-down routine pays off most.

content.todaysFocus: With the wind-down routine in place, today is about reading Avi's wake-window patterns. At 6 to 12 weeks most infants tolerate 60-to-90-minute wake windows across four to five naps; logging a few days reveals his.

actionItems.body: Log every wake window and nap length for the next two to three days; by 12 to 14 weeks the pattern firms up enough to anchor a loose schedule rather than guessing at tired cues.
Protect the first nap of the day, which is usually the easiest to install and sets the rhythm for the rest of the day.
If he skips a nap, bank the lost sleep at the next sleep period with an earlier bedtime by 30 to 60 minutes rather than a late-afternoon makeup nap.

watchFors: [low concern] Variable nap quality day to day, and 30-to-45-minute catnaps; both are typical at 2 to 4 months and age out around 5 to 6 months.
[monitor] Asymmetric movement or a persistent head-turn to one side; raise it at the next visit if repositioning does not resolve it.
[call within 24h] Persistent vomiting unrelated to any recent vaccine, or a clear drop in wet-diaper output.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, seizure-like activity, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 if his lips look blue!

enrichment.body: Keep the sleep log running for a few days; the wake-window pattern stabilizes by 12 to 14 weeks and is what lets you anchor a loose daily schedule.
Vary the tummy-time surface (firm mat, your lap, a slight incline) and keep a toy just out of reach to drive scooting and stretching effort.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

enrichment.body: Play the Suzuki Book 1 recording during a calm awake window; pre-instrument listening exposure can begin now at no cost and primes the mother-tongue listening approach.

upcoming: Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; the log you build now feeds directly into it.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).
Around week 14-18: the 4-month sleep regression typically begins; baseline data on his current windows will make the shift easier to read.

subject: Day 68: swiping at the play gym

content.todaysFocus: Reaching is shifting from accidental to deliberate. Today is about giving Avi a play gym set up so his swipes at hanging toys turn into purposeful, repeatable practice.

actionItems.body: Hang two or three toys at swat height on the play gym so his arms make contact when he reaches; deliberate batting at this age builds the reach-and-grasp foundation that consolidates over the next couple of months.
actionItems.sourceLabel: AAP HealthyChildren: movement, birth to 3 months

actionItems.body: Rotate the toys you hang every few days so the visual and motor targets stay novel rather than ignored.
Keep total container time (bouncer, swing, car seat outside the car) under 2 hours per day so floor and play-gym time stays the default.

watchFors: [low concern] Non-painful spit-up and frequent hand-sucking during play; both are routine at this stage.
[monitor] Movement that consistently favors one side, or hands that stay fisted without occasionally opening; note it for the next visit.
[call within 24h] A feeding refusal lasting more than 24 hours, or a new persistent crying pattern with no clear trigger.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, sudden limpness, apnea, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 right away for blue lips!

enrichment.body: Hang toys at swat height on the play gym and let him practice deliberate reaching and swiping; this is the motor work that bridges into grasping.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP HealthyChildren: movement, birth to 3 months

enrichment.body: Set a toy swinging and let him track it; vary the colors and shapes you hang to keep his fluid visual tracking engaged.
Narrate his hits and misses in real time (you got it, almost, try again) so the language stream stays tied to what his body is doing.

upcoming: Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; keep the wind-down routine steady.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).
Around week 14-18: 4-month sleep regression on the horizon; reaching and rolling often emerge alongside it.

content.todaysFocus: Tempo and rhythm discrimination is sharpening this week. Today is about stretching Avi's perceptual range with live, varied-tempo singing before it narrows to the rhythms he hears most.

actionItems.body: Sing live to him in a tempo sequence today (a slow lullaby, then a fast clapping song, then slow again); live participatory music, not recordings, is the active ingredient tied to earlier rhythm and pitch discrimination.

Take a 20-to-30-minute daylight stroller loop for fresh air and parental cardiovascular recovery; keep giving the 400 IU/day vitamin D supplement regardless, since breastfed infants need it independent of sun exposure.
If you and Anoushka have not yet, talk through the first-birthday venue and date now, since top Bay Area venues book 6 to 9 months out.

watchFors: [low concern] Quiet startle to loud sounds and reactive head-turns toward voices; both are expected and reassuring.
[monitor] Persistent head asymmetry (positional plagiocephaly) despite repositioning; ask about PT or repositioning advice at the next visit.
[call within 24h] Decreased feeding over 24 hours or more, or any new color change during feeds.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, seizure-like activity, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 immediately for blue lips!

enrichment.body: Sing a slow lullaby, then a fast clapping song, then slow again; varying tempo live preserves the perceptual range as his rhythm discrimination sharpens.
Add a book with a repeated refrain to the rotation; the predictable pattern drives early predictive language processing alongside the novel titles.
Fit in a daylight stroller loop for varied sensory input and vitamin D, keeping the 400 IU/day supplement going since outdoor time does not replace it for breastfed infants.

upcoming: Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; keep the wind-down sequence consistent.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).
Around week 14-18: the 4-month sleep regression typically begins, often alongside the first roll.
